world.bio: I build about fourteen acoustic guitars a year in a rented workshop in Footscray. Steel-string, mostly dreadnoughts and OMs, with Sitka spruce tops and Australian timbers for backs and sides: blackwood, Tasmanian myrtle, sometimes silky oak. I have a waiting list of about a year and a half, and I keep losing builds to unstable wood. My partner is pregnant with our first.
skills_assets: Twelve years of building and repair, apprenticed under a luthier in Brunswick
A workshop of 60 square metres in Footscray with a spray booth and a dust extractor
A waiting list of 22 clients, average price 7,500 Australian dollars per guitar
Instrument sales through word of mouth and a modest Instagram following of 6,000
A moisture meter and a humidity-controlled wood room
Relationships with a few Melbourne tonewood suppliers

projects.name: Commission queue
projects.text: Fourteen guitars this year, nine finished. Five on the bench. I scrapped two sets this year because the backs moved after bracing; the wood was new-growth blackwood that had not seasoned enough, and the stock moves too much with Melbourne's humidity swings. I cannot get properly aged blackwood for guitar backs anymore.

projects.name: Workshop ventilation
projects.text: The landlord is arguing about the extraction vent I installed. He says it breaks the lease, I say the lacquer fumes are a health issue. My lawyer wrote a letter. Maybe we compromise.

projects.name: Baby prep
projects.text: Our first baby is due in January. We need to move the guitar parts out of the second bedroom.

notes.text: Opened a set of blackwood I bought in March: the board has cupped in the humidity. Two weeks of work in the bin. My supplier said new-growth is all there is now. I said I need old growth. He said so does everyone.
Thursday bluegrass at the pub: I played banjo for three songs and forgot the bridge on 'Rocky Top'. The bassist laughed and said no one noticed.
Wife Lena had her 20-week scan. Everything looks fine. I got teary in the car park. I'm building a guitar for the baby; spruce top, small body.
Landlord came to the workshop and pointed at the vent. He said it was not in the lease. I said neither was the smell of lacquer in the neighbours' yards. He grumbled.

Customer Emma on the waitlist sent a message asking where the wood is from. She loves stories. She said she once bought a violin because the maker told her the spruce was from a barn in Bavaria. I told her about the blackwood but not about the problem.

Saw an old terrace house being demolished in Carlton. The beams on the skip looked like blackwood and Baltic pine. I stopped and stared. The foreman said, 'Not for sale, mate, they're nailed to bits.'
Spoke to a friend who builds furniture. He said you need someone with a resaw to open up old beams. I don't have a bandsaw of that size, and nails would wreck my blades.

A customer on the waitlist said they love provenance. 'A guitar from a Carlton terrace built in 1890' would sell itself, he said. I laughed, but it's true. People pay for a story, if the sound is good.
Making a list of things I need before the baby arrives: more orders finished, the vent sorted, aged wood sourced. The third is hardest.

messages.text:
Greg: Got a new lot of blackwood in, but it is plantation stock.
Me: How old?
Greg: Maybe thirty years. Moisture 11 percent.
Me: Pass, thanks.

Landlord: I need the vent removed by the end of the month.
Me: I have a letter from my lawyer.
Landlord: We'll talk.

Emma: Where is the wood for my guitar from?
Me: Australian blackwood, I'm sourcing the best I can.
Emma: Love that. Any story to go with it?

Lena: The nursery paint arrived. Where do I put the bridge clamps?
Me: Anywhere but the baby's room.

calendar.event: Meeting with the landlord about the vent
Delivery of two guitars to customers

relations.about: Midwife, 31 weeks pregnant, patient with sawdust in the house.
Tonewood dealer, kind, wary of old-growth rules.
Does reclaimed-timber tables, knows who has bandsaws.

constraints: Cannot take new orders until the wood issue is sorted
Needs wood with stable moisture, preferably decades old
Wants to avoid ethically dubious old-growth sources
sensitive: Income has been irregular; two scrapped sets cost around 3,000 dollars in materials
Worried about balancing the baby, rent and work

disclosure_policy.t1_after_signal: His customers care about wood provenance and stories.
